status: V2 · historical hypothesis research · partial four-sport coverage

drivers.factor: Cold vs hot (source units; not cross-league)

joint_drivers.note: Complete-case association, standardized variables; not causal; uncertainty not estimated.

research_v2.question: Has home advantage declined over time?
research_v2.method: OLS trend across completed season estimates
research_v2.detail: Negative means decline; seasons weighted equally.

research_v2.question: Is it greater in the postseason?
research_v2.detail: Regular-season team strengths held fixed. Selection and seeding remain potential confounders.

research_v2.question: Is it most valuable between evenly matched teams?
research_v2.method: Constant log-odds model: lift by strength band
research_v2.detail: Mathematical probability effect; does not establish a varying home coefficient.

research_v2.question: Are team and stadium effects persistent?
research_v2.detail: At least 20 home games in both halves; midpoint season 2013. Not independent of retrospective ratings.

research_v2.question: Does near-full capacity amplify advantage?
research_v2.detail: Insufficient eligible observations: 0 and 0. Absolute attendance is not stadium fullness or measured noise.

research_v2.question: Do rivalries amplify advantage?
research_v2.detail: Division games are not necessarily rivalries.

research_v2.question: Is advantage larger at night?
research_v2.detail: NFL time is Eastern kickoff time, not venue-local time; MLB source marks day/night.

research_v2.question: Does crossing time zones matter more than distance?
research_v2.method: Joint standardized association of visitor time-zone crossings and distance
research_v2.detail: Positive means time-zone coefficient larger in magnitude; metro proxies, not itineraries. Strong collinearity and no causal claim.

research_v2.question: Does eastward travel differ from westward travel?
research_v2.detail: Metro and standard time-zone proxies; does not observe itinerary or jet lag.

research_v2.question: Does extra visitor rest erase home advantage?
research_v2.detail: Calendar-day rest, no injury or recovery measurements.

research_v2.question: Do extended road trips hurt visitors?
research_v2.detail: Insufficient eligible observations: 4513 and 0. Same-day doubleheaders excluded. Schedule streak is not proof of continuous travel.

research_v2.question: Does the first home game after a long trip hurt the host?
research_v2.detail: Negative means worse after a long road stretch.

research_v2.question: Is advantage larger in late periods?
research_v2.detail: Existing game-level sources do not supply comparable late-period outcomes.

research_v2.question: Does crowd noise benefit home defense more than offense?
research_v2.detail: Requires drive/play-level offense and defense with crowd exposure; final scores cannot isolate noise.

research_v2.question: Do visitors commit more pre-snap penalties?
research_v2.detail: Requires pre-snap penalty opportunities and penalty attribution.

research_v2.question: Do subjective officiating calls favor hosts?
research_v2.detail: Requires subjective calls and comparable opportunities; umpire identity alone is insufficient.

research_v2.question: Does high altitude amplify advantage against low-altitude visitors?
research_v2.detail: Approximate metro elevation, >=1200m vs <300m; not physiological acclimation.

research_v2.question: Does playing style modify advantage?
research_v2.detail: A scoring environment proxy, not measured playing style or pace.

research_v2.question: Is home improvement or away decline the larger mechanism?
research_v2.method: Separate scoring model relative to designated neutral games
research_v2.detail: Positive means home scoring increase exceeds away scoring decrease; neutral games selected nonrandomly, small sample, no causal interpretation.

research_v2.question: Has conference realignment increased home advantage?
research_v2.detail: Not applicable: original hypothesis concerns college football conference realignment.

attribution: The information used here was obtained free of charge from and is copyrighted by Retrosheet. Interested parties may contact Retrosheet at 20 Sunset Rd., Newark, DE 19711.
limitations: Game-level observational adjustment is not a causal decomposition.

V2 contrasts use unadjusted-for-multiplicity season-cluster intervals conditional on retrospective strengths. Metro estimates are proxies; no actual travel itineraries or venue elevations are observed.
Divisional games are a rivalry proxy; combined scoring is a style proxy; absolute attendance does not measure occupancy.
NBA seasons are labeled by starting year. MLB alternate sites are excluded using inferred primary home venue; neutral MLB games unavailable.
Team and stadium rankings use a 40-game shrinkage prior; stadium identifiers are source IDs.
Season-cluster interval requires at least five seasons. Annual estimates have no interval.
Driver contrasts do not jointly adjust for other drivers; they are exploratory.
No predictions or betting advice. Simulator uses hypothetical neutral odds, not live team forecasts.

All 20 questions have explicit results or unavailable statuses for each calculated sport. College football is unavailable because the CollegeFootballData API key was not configured. No missing result is interpreted as zero effect.

Travel geography is an approximate manually curated city-level mapping, not an audited historical venue database. Time-zone offsets omit daylight-saving exceptions; treat results as sensitivity/proxy evidence.
Season-cluster intervals are exploratory and conditional on retrospectively estimated team strengths; not multiplicity-adjusted. Model-based effects are not causal.
